name: Bunnytaur
body:
Bunnytaurs are rarely seen by other races outside of their warrens. This is not due to any sort of ill will or bigotry—it’s simply because bunnytaurs, being both fecund and delicious, make very popular prey for hungry monsters. This has filled the species with a preternatural fear that they struggle to overcome.

Physical Description: Bunnytaurs stand almost four feet tall. They have the upper bodies of halfling-like humanoids, with pointed elven ears and dark eyes, and the lower bodies of giant furry rabbits. They are fairly plump all around. Their hair is usually done up in elaborate braids or knots to keep it away from their eyes and ears.

Society: Bunnytaurs dwell in warrens, either woven out of thorny forest briars or dug out of the prairie soil. Some live in the sides of cliffs. They are a fairly mobile species, traveling every year—sometimes every season—to avoid predation, and larger warrens have multiple permanent residences established that they move between.

Bunnytaurs’ exact societal systems can vary, but they are generally very loose dictatorships or oligarchies, with the leader or leaders occasionally exerting iron-fisted control to keep the whole warren safe. This control is largely unenforced, however, and a warren that turns against their leader falls back on a herd mentality to make decisions. That herd mentality is almost always quite cowardly. When a warren grows too large, the bunnytaurs select a number to send out to start a new warren. This group is comprised of bolder younger bunnytaurs (who tend to have less social status with which to resist the decision).

Relations: Bunnytaurs are cautious, but polite, and do trade with most friendly races. Sadly, their fear tends to sabotage any lasting friendships. They get along best with dwarves, who can help them construct defenses. Dwarves rarely push for closer relationships, and that’s how the bunnytaurs like it. Elves often try to protect bunnytaur warrens as best they can without getting too close, and bunnytaurs regard elves as fearsome wardens of the wilderness. Gnomes come on a bit strong, and those of human blood are frequently too rough for the fearful bunnytaurs. Halflings find the cowardly bunnytaurs… frustrating. Bunnytaurs don’t want to hurt anyone. All they want to do is survive, and this can lead them to a somewhat insulated existence. Their social mores and spiritual beliefs sharply vary—some warrens exhibit virtually no taboos, while others are locked into rigid superstitions and rules. The one constant, however, is the groupthink they invariably fall back upon, and so most bunnytaurs lean towards lawful neutral. They favor gods of community, as well as traveler gods to look after nomadic warrens.

Adventurers: Adventuring is a frightening prospect for many bunnytaurs, but there are many who wish to overcome their innate flight impulse and learn to fight back. Those who are sent out to start new warrens tend to be the boldest of the lot, eager to scout out a new haven for their people. Additionally, it is not uncommon for a bunnytaur to become separated from the others due to a panicked flight or worse tragedy.

Core Traits (15 RP)
Ability Score Modifiers: Bunnytaurs are nimble and likable, but they are also cowardly and weak-willed. They gain +2 Dexterity, +2 Charisma, and –2 Wisdom.
Type: Bunnytaurs are monstrous humanoids. 3 RP
Size: Bunnytaurs are Small creatures and gain a +1 size bonus to their AC, a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a –1 penalty to their combat maneuver checks and CMD, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks.
Speed: Bunnytaurs have a base speed of 40 feet. 1 RP
Languages: Bunnytaurs begin play knowing their native tongue, Bunnese, a chirpy, extremely high-context language. Bunnytaurs with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Common, Dwarven, Goblin, and Orc.
Other Traits
Huddle: When prone, a bunnytaur automatically huddles its humanoid upper body down against its furry lower half (even if unconscious). It gains a +4 circumstance bonus on Fortitude saves against cold effects and a +1 racial bonus on Will saves against fear effects while prone. Standing up does not provoke attacks of opportunities for a bunnytaur, and a bunnytaur can jump while prone as if it was standing. 3 RP
Self-Preservation: Bunnytaurs gain a +2 racial bonus on Will saves to resist enchantments that compel them to carry out violent or life-threatening acts, such as attacking allies or entering a burning building. Acts such as surrendering to hungry goblins do not trigger this bonus. 1 RP
Creeper: Bunnytaurs gain a +1 racial bonus to Perception and Stealth checks, and Perception and Stealth are always class skills for them. 3 RP
Powerful Jumper: When a bunnytaur makes a high or long jump, the DC for that jump is halved. In addition, bunnytaurs gain Jumper as a bonus feat (Bunnytaurs are always considered to have a running start when making Acrobatics checks to jump). 3 RP
Sprint: Bunnytaurs gain Run as a bonus feat at first level. 1 RP
Forest Stride: Bunnytaurs can move through any sort of undergrowth (such as natural thorns, briars, overgrown areas, and similar terrain) at their normal speed and without taking damage or suffering any other impairment. Thorns, briars, and overgrown areas that have been magically manipulated to impede motion, however, still affect them. 1 RP
Senses: Darkvision. Bunnytaurs can see perfectly in darkness up to 60 feet.
Terror: Bunnytaurs take a –4 penalty on saves against fear effects. When a bunnytaur succeeds on a save against a fear effect, it is still shaken for 1 round. If the bunnytaur is unable to act in a surprise round, it becomes shaken for 1 minute. When a bunnytaur is frightened or panicked, it gains a +20 enhancement bonus to its base land speed. –3 RP
Quadruped: Bunnytaurs possess four legs and two arms, granting them a +4 racial bonus to CMD against trip attempts. 2 RP
Alternate Racial Traits

The following racial traits may be selected instead of existing bunnytaur traits.

Bramble Weaver: Not all bunnytaurs are tunnel diggers. Some stick to the bramble thickets and rose briars, spending all their lives trying to keep their bushy tails from getting snagged. These bunnytaurs gain low-light vision and have the ability to converse with briars and thornbushes, as if subject to a continual speak with plants spell. This replaces the sprint and darkvision traits.
Burrow: Some bunnytaurs are more focused on warren digging than jumping. These bunnytaurs gain a burrow speed of 10 feet. Bunnytaurs with this trait do not gain the forest stride or powerful jumper traits.
Ready to Bolt: Constant fear makes some bunnytaurs even more alert to danger—and terrified of ever staying in one place for too long. These bunnytaurs gain a +2 bonus on initiative checks. Bunnytaurs with this trait do not gain the huddle trait.
Sharp Hearing: Some bunnytaurs have especially long, rabbit-like ears, and gain a +4 racial bonus on Perception checks involving hearing. Perception is always a class skill for them. Bunnytaurs with this trait do not gain the creeper trait.
